20	// maxSyncAttempts bounds in-process retries for transient git-fetch failures.
21	// Production measurement over 14 days of @entire.sync.attempts on mirror.sync
22	// spans showed attempt 1 = 147,132 syncs, attempt 2 = 3,573 (2.4% of attempt 1
23	// continued), attempt 3 = 862 (24% of attempt 2 continued) — under the old
24	// 3-attempt budget, that attempt-3 tail left ~1.2 terminal 404s/day. The two
25	// continuation rates differ by an order of magnitude, so the decay beyond
26	// attempt 3 isn't known and a precise residual-failure estimate at 8 attempts
27	// isn't supported by this data; widening the budget is expected to clear
28	// materially more of the attempt-3 tail without a confident number attached.
29	const maxSyncAttempts = 8
30	
31	// syncRetryDelay paces in-process retries. The shortest observed gap between
32	// a 404 and a successful sibling sync of the same repo was ~3s, so a 2s
33	// delay sits just under that boundary — long enough for GitHub's git edge
34	// to settle after a mint, short enough to stay responsive. Kept fixed (no
35	// exponential backoff): the continuation rates behind maxSyncAttempts were
36	// measured at this exact spacing, so changing it would invalidate that data.
37	const syncRetryDelay = 2 * time.Second
38	
39	// unmirroredRefPrefix marks branches that live only in Entire and are never
40	// mirrored to/from GitHub. Excluding it from the sync scope also excludes it
41	// from prune, so a GitHub→Entire sync can't delete an unmirrored branch that
42	// (by definition) has no counterpart on the source. This is the inbound half
43	// of the contract; the outbound half (skipping push-through) lives in
44	// entiredb's server/githttp. entiredb pins the same literal as
45	// mirror.UnmirroredRefPrefix — kept in lockstep here because the two live in
46	// separate Go modules. See entiredb docs/adrs/20260702-unmirrored-branches.md.
47	const unmirroredRefPrefix = "refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/"
48	
49	// namespaceRefPrefix is the Entire-owned ref namespace (COR-1563). entiredb's
50	// writer scope refuses a push to it that does not declare the namespace sync
51	// kind, so a GitHub-kind sync — AllRefs + prune — must exclude it, or it plans
52	// a delete of every namespace ref the target holds and fails on every
53	// redelivery. entiredb pins the same literal as forge.NativeRefPrefix; kept in
54	// lockstep here because the two live in separate Go modules.
55	const namespaceRefPrefix = "refs/heads/entire/native/"
56	
57	// reservedAncestorRefs are the bare directory-anchor refs entiredb blocks from
58	// creation so the namespace beneath each stays usable: a leaf ref squatting an
59	// anchor would directory/file-conflict with every ref under it. entiredb
60	// rejects a push to any of them, so the worker must skip them on inbound sync
61	// or a source repo that happens to carry one would fail the whole mirror.
62	// These are exact-match (ExcludeRefs), NOT prefixes, so a normal ref like
63	// refs/heads/entire/a or refs/meta/entire/main still passes this filter.
64	//
65	// The refs/heads/* pair protects the unmirrored-branches feature (entiredb
66	// docs/adrs/20260702-unmirrored-branches.md); the refs/meta pair are base
67	// anchors entiredb reserves for EVERY caller — a workload carve-out matches by
68	// prefix + "/" and so never reaches the bare anchor. Keep in lockstep with the
69	// reservedExact set in entiredb's refpolicy/refpolicy.go.
70	var reservedAncestorRefs = []string{
71		"refs/heads/entire",
72		"refs/heads/entire/unmirrored",
73		"refs/meta",
74		"refs/meta/entire",
75	}
76	
77	// excludeRefPrefixes are the source ref namespaces the worker never mirrors
78	// (and, being unmirrored, never prunes) on a GITHUB sync. Shared between the
79	// sync scope and the default-branch reconcile guard: a source HEAD under one
80	// of these prefixes can never land on the target, so the reconcile treats it
81	// as non-convergent rather than looping forever (see isNonMirrorableBranch —
82	// which deliberately keeps checking THIS list for both kinds, because
83	// entiredb's SetDefaultBranch rejects an unmirrored-namespace default
84	// unconditionally). The refs/heads/ entries here are the only ones a HEAD
85	// could point at; the rest are kept for a single source of truth with the
86	// sync scope. entiredb-kind syncs use excludeRefPrefixesFor, which drops
87	// exactly one entry.
88	var excludeRefPrefixes = []string{
89		"refs/pull/",
90		"refs/heads/trunk-merge/",
91		"refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/",
92		"refs/tlog/",
93		"refs/remotes/",
94		"refs/internal/",
95		"refs/replace/",
96		"refs/bisect/",
97	
98		// Only Entire's own managed sub-namespace is reserved, NOT all of
99		// refs/meta/. entiredb reserves refs/meta/entire/* (refpolicy's
100		// ManagedMetaPrefix) and carves it out for the entire-api workload alone,
101		// which the worker is not — so the worker must still skip it. The rest of
102		// refs/meta/* is unreserved by design: standard git-meta clients push
103		// refs/meta/config and friends directly, and those mirror like any other
104		// ref. See entiredb refpolicy/refpolicy.go and its ADR
105		// docs/adrs/20260603-reserved-refs.md.
106		"refs/meta/entire/",
107	
108		"refs/namespaces/",
109		"refs/stash", // covers the exact refs/stash ref and refs/stash/*
110	
111		// refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/* are Entire-only branches (see
112		// unmirroredRefPrefix). Excluded so Prune never deletes one for being
113		// absent on GitHub; the outbound push-through skip that keeps them off
114		// GitHub lives in entiredb.
115		unmirroredRefPrefix,
116	}
117	
118	// githubExcludeRefPrefixes is the GitHub-kind scope: excludeRefPrefixes plus
119	// the Entire-owned namespace. Kept OUT of excludeRefPrefixes itself because
120	// that list also backs the kind-blind isNonMirrorableBranch, and entiredb
121	// reserves the namespace on GitHub-mirror rows only — a native mirror may
122	// carry a namespace branch as its default and its HEAD must follow it. A
123	// GitHub HEAD there needs no local guard: entiredb answers SetDefaultBranch
124	// with InvalidArgument, which recoveryIsPermanent already terminates on.
125	var githubExcludeRefPrefixes = append(append([]string(nil), excludeRefPrefixes...), namespaceRefPrefix)
126	
127	// namespaceRefAnchor is the bare directory anchor of the Entire-owned
128	// namespace. It is not covered by namespaceRefPrefix (no trailing slash) and
129	// entiredb's writer scope refuses it on a GitHub-mirror row exactly like the
130	// refs beneath it, so both kinds that touch such a row must exclude it
131	// exactly — as a prefix it would also swallow refs/heads/entire/nativeish.
132	const namespaceRefAnchor = "refs/heads/entire/native"
133	
134	// excludeRefsWithAnchor is reservedAncestorRefs plus the namespace anchor, for
135	// the two kinds that write a GitHub-mirror row.
136	var excludeRefsWithAnchor = append(append([]string(nil), reservedAncestorRefs...), namespaceRefAnchor)
137	
138	// includeRefPrefixesFor returns the namespaces a kind may manage, or nil for
139	// the unnarrowed kinds. It is the whole defence for a namespace sync: git-sync
140	// neither pushes nor prunes a ref outside the returned set.
141	func includeRefPrefixesFor(kind gitjobs.SourceKind) []string {
142		if kind == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDBNamespace {
143			return []string{namespaceRefPrefix}
144		}
145		return nil
146	}
147	
148	// excludeRefsFor returns the exact-match sync-scope exclusions for a kind. Only
149	// the entiredb kind keeps the bare list: on a native row the anchor is an
150	// ordinary branch name entiredb reserves nothing beneath.
151	func excludeRefsFor(kind gitjobs.SourceKind) []string {
152		if kind == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB {
153			return reservedAncestorRefs
154		}
155		return excludeRefsWithAnchor
156	}
157	
158	// excludeRefPrefixesFor returns the sync-scope exclusions for a source kind.
159	// A GitHub-kind sync additionally excludes the Entire-owned namespace (see
160	// githubExcludeRefPrefixes). An entiredb-kind sync (native mirroring) drops
161	// exactly the unmirrored-namespace exclusion and nothing else (plan decision
162	// 3, ADR 20260720-native-mirroring): that exclusion exists to keep Entire-only
163	// branches out of a GitHub round-trip, and when the source IS entiredb the
164	// namespace replicates like any branch — a native mirror is a full read-only
165	// copy. Everything else stays excluded for the same reasons as GitHub:
166	// refs/tlog/* is per-placement entiredb-owned state receive-pack rejects,
167	// and the reserved namespaces would 403 the push.
168	func excludeRefPrefixesFor(kind gitjobs.SourceKind) []string {
169		if kind == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDBNamespace {
170			// Scoped by inclusion, not exclusion: every ref outside the namespace is
171			// already out of scope, including git-sync's own bootstrap markers,
172			// which take their scope from the branch they checkpoint.
173			return nil
174		}
175		if kind != gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB {
176			return githubExcludeRefPrefixes
177		}
178		out := make([]string, 0, len(excludeRefPrefixes)-1)
179		for _, p := range excludeRefPrefixes {
180			if p != unmirroredRefPrefix {
181				out = append(out, p)
182			}
183		}
184		return out
185	}

297	func newSyncer(cfg syncerConfig) (*syncer, error) {
298		// The cluster trust boundary is either explicitly configured
299		// (cfg.targetClusterHost — set from resolveTargetClusterHost when
300		// ENTIRE_TARGET_INTERNAL_URL diverges from the audience URL) or
301		// derived from targetBaseURL. When ENTIRE_TARGET_URL points at the
302		// cluster entry domain (royalcanin.partial.to), the host is the
303		// FQDN itself and nodeN.royalcanin.partial.to matches as a subdomain
304		// — so the info/refs 307 redirect carries auth headers through.
305		// Pointing at a specific node (node1.royalcanin.partial.to) narrows
306		// the trust boundary to that one node — info/refs 307s to sibling
307		// nodes will lose auth, which is acceptable for debug/rollback but
308		// not for steady-state operation.
309		clusterHost := cfg.targetClusterHost
310		if clusterHost == "" {
311			derived, err := targetBaseURLHost(cfg.targetBaseURL)
312			if err != nil {
313				return nil, err
314			}
315			clusterHost = derived
316		}
317	
318		// GitHub source fetches MUST ride a public-CA transport — the internal
319		// mTLS transport's RootCAs only trust the cluster CA and would fail
320		// x509 verification on github.com. Target pushes — and, per sync,
321		// entiredb source fetches (see httpClientFor) — ride
322		// cfg.targetTransport (svctok mTLS) when configured. Split so the two
323		// paths can't conflict; clusterTransport routes by destination host.
324		sourceBase := otelhttp.NewTransport(
325			http.DefaultTransport,
326			otelhttp.WithSpanNameFormatter(gitSmartHTTPSpanName),
327		)
328		var clusterBase http.RoundTripper
329		if cfg.targetTransport != nil {
330			clusterBase = otelhttp.NewTransport(
331				cfg.targetTransport,
332				otelhttp.WithSpanNameFormatter(gitSmartHTTPSpanName),
333			)
334		}
335		targetClusters := []string{clusterHost}
336		targetEntryHost, err := entryHostPort(cfg.targetBaseURL)
337		if err != nil {
338			return nil, err
339		}
340		entryHosts := []string{targetEntryHost}
341		replicas := newReplicaCache()
342		transport := &clusterTransport{
343			clusters:    targetClusters,
344			entryHosts:  entryHosts,
345			base:        sourceBase,
346			clusterBase: clusterBase,
347			replicas:    replicas,
348			metrics:     cfg.metrics,
349		}
350	
351		return &syncer{
352			bootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes: cfg.bootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes,
353			httpClient:                    &http.Client{Transport: transport},
354			sourceBaseURL:                 cfg.sourceBaseURL,
355			targetBaseURL:                 cfg.targetBaseURL,
356			targetClusters:                targetClusters,
357			publicBase:                    sourceBase,
358			clusterBase:                   clusterBase,
359			replicas:                      replicas,
360			entryHosts:                    entryHosts,
361			githubApp:                     cfg.githubApp,
362			metrics:                       cfg.metrics,
363			repoAdmin:                     cfg.repoAdmin,
364		}, nil
365	}

367	// httpClientFor returns the HTTP client for one sync. github-kind syncs
368	// share the long-lived client (target rides mTLS, github.com rides the
369	// public-CA base). An entiredb-kind sync gets a per-sync client whose
370	// cluster set additionally trusts the consume-time admitted source cluster
371	// parent — so the fetch, and the per-node hosts the source cluster's
372	// /info/refs 307s to, present the client cert (the whole credential: the
373	// source's svctok listener grants the workload cert-only cluster-wide pull).
374	// The raw SourceURL never expands this trust set. With no mTLS transport
375	// configured (dev/loadtest single-URL setups) the per-sync client degrades to
376	// the shared public base exactly like target pushes do.
377	func (s *syncer) httpClientFor(req syncRequest) *http.Client {
378		if !req.entiredbSourced() {
379			return s.httpClient
380		}
381		clusters := append([]string{req.SourceClusterParent}, s.targetClusters...)
382		// The source's svctok host is an entry host for this sync: its
383		// /info/refs 307s off non-hosting nodes exactly like the target's, and
384		// its replica set is cached under its own key. Admission has already
385		// validated SourceURL's shape, so a parse failure here just leaves the
386		// source uncached rather than failing the sync.
387		entryHosts := s.entryHosts
388		if h, err := entryHostPort(req.SourceURL); err == nil {
389			entryHosts = append([]string{h}, s.entryHosts...)
390		}
391		var rt http.RoundTripper = &clusterTransport{
392			clusters:    clusters,
393			entryHosts:  entryHosts,
394			base:        s.publicBase,
395			clusterBase: s.clusterBase,
396			replicas:    s.replicas,
397			metrics:     s.metrics,
398		}
399		if req.namespaceScoped() {
400			rt = &syncKindTransport{base: rt, kind: syncKindNamespace, clusters: s.targetClusters}
401		}
402		return &http.Client{Transport: rt}
403	}

405	// entryHostPort returns the host:port of a cluster entry URL exactly as it
406	// appears in the URLs git-sync builds from it (url.URL.Host), which is what
407	// clusterTransport.entryHosts is matched against.
408	func entryHostPort(rawURL string) (string, error) {
409		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
410		if err != nil {
411			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse entry URL %q: %w", rawURL, err)
412		}
413		if u.Hostname() == "" {
414			return "", fmt.Errorf("entry URL %q has no host", rawURL)
415		}
416		return u.Host, nil
417	}

419	// retryTransientFetch runs fn, retrying up to maxSyncAttempts on a transient
420	// git-fetch 404 — the same intermittent GitHub /info/refs failure the main
421	// sync loop absorbs (see isTransientGitFetchError). The default-branch
422	// recovery reuses it for its source-HEAD probe and its re-run replicate so a
423	// one-in-thirty blip on those extra GitHub reads is retried in-process rather
424	// than surfacing a raw "http 404" that the permanent-status classifier would
425	// promote to a terminal failure — the exact wedge the main loop's retry
426	// exists to prevent. A non-transient error returns immediately; a persistent
427	// transient error returns after the attempts are spent, matching the main
428	// loop's contract that an exhausted 404 is then permanent.
429	func retryTransientFetch[T any](ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) (T, error)) (T, error) {
430		var zero T
431		var lastErr error
432		for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxSyncAttempts; attempt++ {
433			if attempt > 1 {
434				select {
435				case <-ctx.Done():
436					return zero, ctx.Err()
437				case <-time.After(syncRetryDelay):
438				}
439			}
440			v, err := fn(ctx)
441			if err == nil {
442				return v, nil
443			}
444			lastErr = err
445			if !isTransientGitFetchError(err) {
446				return zero, err
447			}
448		}
449		return zero, lastErr
450	}

452	func targetBaseURLHost(rawURL string) (string, error) {
453		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
454		if err != nil {
455			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse target URL %q: %w", rawURL, err)
456		}
457		// Check Hostname() rather than Host: a port-only form like "https://:8080"
458		// gives Host=":8080" (non-empty) but Hostname()="" — which would silently
459		// make hostInCluster always false and fail every push with 401.
460		if u.Hostname() == "" {
461			return "", fmt.Errorf("target URL %q has no host", rawURL)
462		}
463		return u.Hostname(), nil
464	}

466	func (s *syncer) sync(ctx context.Context, req syncRequest) error {
467		sourceURL := s.sourceURL(req)
468		targetURL := s.targetURL(req)
469	
470		ctx, span := Tracer().Start(ctx, "mirror.sync",
471			trace.WithAttributes(
472				attribute.String("entire.source_kind", string(req.kind())),
473				attribute.String("entire.source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
474				attribute.String("entire.source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
475				attribute.String("entire.target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
476				attribute.Int64("entire.installation_id", req.InstallationID),
477				attribute.String("entire.source_url", sourceURL),
478				attribute.String("entire.target_url", targetURL),
479			),
480		)
481		defer span.End()
482	
483		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Starting git-sync",
484			slog.String("source_kind", string(req.kind())),
485			slog.String("source", sourceURL),
486			slog.String("target", targetURL),
487			slog.Int64("installation_id", req.InstallationID),
488		)
489	
490		auth, err := s.sourceAuth(ctx, req)
491		if err != nil {
492			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", 1))
493			classified := classifySyncError(fmt.Errorf("resolving source auth: %w", err))
494			span.RecordError(classified)
495			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "source auth")
496			return classified
497		}
498	
499		// The token is minted once and reused across retries: the working theory
500		// for the transient 404 is GitHub's eventual consistency between
501		// api.github.com (where the token is minted) and github.com (where the
502		// git fetch uses it). Waiting lets that token propagate. Re-minting
503		// would reset the propagation clock with a fresh token, defeating the
504		// purpose of the backoff.
505		client := gitsync.New(gitsync.Options{
506			HTTPClient:                    s.httpClientFor(req),
507			BootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes: s.bootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes,
508			Auth:                          auth,
509			BootstrapLogger: slog.Default().With(
510				slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
511				slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
512				slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo)),
513		})
514	
515		replicateReq := gitsync.SyncRequest{
516			// An entiredb source cluster 307s /info/refs off a non-hosting
517			// node exactly like the target does, so carry the redirect into
518			// the endpoint for entiredb-kind fetches; GitHub never emits it
519			// and keeps the plain endpoint.
520			Source: gitsync.Endpoint{
521				URL:                    sourceURL,
522				FollowInfoRefsRedirect: req.entiredbSourced(),
523			},
524			// FollowInfoRefsRedirect carries the 307 from a non-hosting
525			// entiredb node into the endpoint, so the subsequent
526			// receive-pack POST lands on the hosting replica instead of
527			// the originally-configured host. No-op for the current
528			// node-specific ENTIRE_TARGET_URL (node1 either hosts or
529			// serves via DISS), but lets us flip fleet to the cluster
530			// entry domain without a code change.
531			Target: gitsync.Endpoint{URL: targetURL, FollowInfoRefsRedirect: true},
532			Scope:  refScopeFor(req),
533			Policy: syncPolicyFor(req),
534		}
535	
536		var (
537			result  gitsync.SyncResult
538			lastErr error
539			attempt int
540		)
541		for attempt = 1; attempt <= maxSyncAttempts; attempt++ {
542			if attempt > 1 {
543				select {
544				case <-ctx.Done():
545					span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", attempt-1))
546					classified := transientErr(ctx.Err())
547					reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, result, classified, ctx.Err(), req)
548					span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "context canceled during retry backoff")
549					return classified
550				case <-time.After(syncRetryDelay):
551				}
552			}
553	
554			result, err = client.Replicate(ctx, replicateReq)
555			if err == nil {
556				lastErr = nil
557				break
558			}
559			lastErr = err
560			if !isTransientGitFetchError(err) {
561				break
562			}
563			if attempt >= maxSyncAttempts {
564				break
565			}
566			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Transient git-fetch failure; will retry",
567				slog.Int("attempt", attempt),
568				slog.Int("max_attempts", maxSyncAttempts),
569				slog.Any("error", redactAuth(err)),
570			)
571		}
572	
573		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", attempt))
574	
575		// A prune delete rejected with entiredb's deny-current-branch reason
576		// means the source renamed its default branch and the mirror's HEAD
577		// hasn't followed: move HEAD via RepoAdmin.SetDefaultBranch, then
578		// re-run the identical replicate in the same job so the stale branch
579		// prunes immediately. This branch is terminal — recovery classifies its
580		// own failures (a transient GitHub 404 during the probe/re-replicate is
581		// retried in-process and stays transient; a non-convergent case such as
582		// an excluded source HEAD or an RPC PermissionDenied is marked permanent
583		// so it stops churning instead of redelivering forever) and returns them
584		// directly, bypassing the generic classifier below. followed tracks that
585		// HEAD was just ensured so the steady-state follow further down skips its
586		// redundant RPC. Already-wedged mirrors heal on their next sync.
587		followed := false
588		if lastErr != nil && s.repoAdmin != nil && !req.namespaceScoped() {
589			if rejectedRef, ok := isDenyCurrentBranchDeletion(lastErr); ok {
590				span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.default_branch_recovery", true))
591				recResult, ensuredHEAD, recErr := s.recoverDefaultBranchRename(ctx, req.TargetULID, rejectedRef,
592					func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
593						probe, perr := retryTransientFetch(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.ProbeResult, error) {
594							return client.Probe(ctx, gitsync.ProbeRequest{Source: gitsync.Endpoint{URL: sourceURL}})
595						})
596						if perr != nil {
597							return "", perr
598						}
599						return probe.SourceHEAD, nil
600					},
601					func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.SyncResult, error) {
602						return retryTransientFetch(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.SyncResult, error) {
603							return client.Replicate(ctx, replicateReq)
604						})
605					},
606				)
607				if recErr != nil {
608					classified := classifyRecoveryError(recErr)
609					span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.sync.default_branch_recovery_error", recoveryErrorCode(recErr)))
610					reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, recoveryReportResult(recResult, result), classified, recErr, req)
611					return classified
612				}
613				result = recResult
614				lastErr = nil
615				// Skip the steady-state follow only when the re-run confirmed the
616				// source HEAD we just ensured. A source that switched its default
617				// AGAIN mid-recovery shows a fresher SourceHEAD on the re-run's
618				// result — fall through to the follow so it is applied now rather
619				// than waiting for the next sync.
620				followed = result.Execution.SourceHEAD == "" || result.Execution.SourceHEAD == ensuredHEAD
621			}
622		}
623	
624		if lastErr != nil {
625			// No refs to apply is a clean no-op, not a failure: don't record it as
626			// a span error and signal the noop disposition so disposeResult acks
627			// rather than redelivering a job that can only repeat the same outcome
628			// against an unchanged source. The reason is recorded but does NOT
629			// change the disposition — every case here acks with no watermark. Only
630			// the diverged case is a standing problem, and it is deliberately
631			// surfaced through the counter and the span rather than through a
632			// failed sync: redelivering it would repeat a refusal that no retry can
633			// resolve, and terminating it would publish 'failed' for a mirror that
634			// is perfectly clonable.
635			if reason, ok := classifyEmptySource(lastErr, req.SourceRefsClaim, req.TargetRefsClaim); ok {
636				// The reason alone is not enough to act on for the uncorroborated
637				// family — one sentinel covers sub-cases with opposite remedies,
638				// separated only by the wrapped message — so the error text rides
639				// on the span and the log, redacted like every other surfaced
640				// sync error.
641				span.SetAttributes(
642					attribute.Bool("entire.sync.noop", true),
643					attribute.String("entire.sync.empty_source_reason", string(reason)),
644					attribute.String("entire.sync.empty_source_error", redactAuth(lastErr).Error()),
645				)
646				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Ok, "no source refs to apply")
647				logEmptySource(ctx, reason, req, lastErr)
648				s.metrics.recordEmptySource(ctx, reason, req.SourceClusterParent)
649				return errSourceNoRefs
650			}
651			classified := classifySyncError(redactAuth(lastErr))
652			reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, result, classified, lastErr, req)
653			return classified
654		}
655	
656		span.SetAttributes(
657			attribute.Int("entire.refs.applied", result.Counts.Applied),
658			attribute.Int("entire.refs.skipped", result.Counts.Skipped),
659			attribute.Int("entire.refs.blocked", result.Counts.Blocked),
660			attribute.Int("entire.refs.deleted", result.Counts.Deleted),
661		)
662	
663		s.reportSyncSuccess(ctx, result, req)
664	
665		// Steady-state follow: a default-branch change to an already-existing
666		// branch produces no data-plane push, so it only ever surfaces here —
667		// as the source HEAD git-sync parsed during the sync. Idempotent
668		// server-side and best-effort (a failure defers to the next sync);
669		// skipped when the recovery path above already ensured HEAD.
670		if !followed && !req.namespaceScoped() {
671			s.followSourceHEAD(ctx, req.TargetULID, result.Execution.SourceHEAD)
672		}
673	
674		return nil
675	}

677	// markSyncSpanResult records a failed sync on the mirror.sync span — except for
678	// a benign concurrent-ref race, which lost a compare-and-swap to a competing
679	// sync of the same repo and self-heals on the next delivery. A race is tagged
680	// entire.sync.raced (queryable, mirroring the mirror.consume carve-out) but left
681	// un-errored, so it never shows as a failed mirror.sync span or counts toward an
682	// error-rate query on this span — matching the outcome metric's nak+term
683	// numerator, which also excludes raced. Exhaustion is a delivery-count concept
684	// the syncer can't see; the consumer still escalates a race that burns through
685	// redelivery to an error on the parent mirror.consume span (see
686	// shouldMarkSpanError). The race check uses the raw error, not the
687	// redacted/classified one, so redactAuth flattening the chain can't defeat it.
688	func markSyncSpanResult(span trace.Span, classified, raw error) {
689		if isConcurrentRefError(raw) {
690			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.raced", true))
691			return
692		}
693		span.RecordError(classified)
694		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "sync from github")
695	}
696	
697	// recoveryReportResult picks which result is worth reporting when the
698	// default-branch reconcile fails.
699	//
700	// Every guard in recoverDefaultBranchRename that bails before re-running
701	// replicate returns a zero SyncResult, so reporting it would log empty
702	// execution attributes and erase the route of the sync that triggered the
703	// reconcile — the one fact reportSyncFailure exists to preserve. The re-run's
704	// result is preferred when it actually ran; otherwise the original failure's
705	// route stands, which is the sync an operator is trying to understand anyway.
706	func recoveryReportResult(recResult, original gitsync.SyncResult) gitsync.SyncResult {
707		if recResult.Execution.OperationMode != "" {
708			return recResult
709		}
710		return original
711	}
712	
713	// reportSyncFailure preserves the execution route git-sync returns alongside
714	// a post-planning error. In particular, a failed batched bootstrap carries the
715	// route that selected bootstrap and the reason relay was unavailable; dropping
716	// the result here made those failures indistinguishable from an ordinary relay
717	// failure in both logs and traces.
718	func reportSyncFailure(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, result gitsync.SyncResult, classified, raw error, req syncRequest) {
719		span.SetAttributes(
720			attribute.String("entire.sync.operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
721			attribute.String("entire.sync.transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
722			attribute.String("entire.sync.relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
723			attribute.Bool("entire.sync.batch.enabled", result.Execution.Batch.Enabled),
724			attribute.Int("entire.sync.batch.planned", result.Execution.Batch.Planned),
725			attribute.Int("entire.sync.batch.done", result.Execution.Batch.Done),
726		)
727		markSyncSpanResult(span, classified, raw)
728	
729		args := []any{
730			slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
731			slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
732			slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
733			slog.String("operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
734			slog.String("transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
735			slog.String("relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
736			slog.Bool("batch_enabled", result.Execution.Batch.Enabled),
737			slog.Int("batch_planned", result.Execution.Batch.Planned),
738			slog.Int("batch_done", result.Execution.Batch.Done),
739			slog.Any("error", classified),
740		}
741		if isConcurrentRefError(raw) {
742			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Git sync execution raced", args...)
743			return
744		}
745		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Git sync execution failed", args...)
746	}

778	// reportSyncSuccess records a completed sync's outcome: the log line, and for a
779	// converged empty pair the counter reason that says the placement healed.
780	//
781	// Extracted from sync() for one reason — nothing could test it there. The
782	// converged branch is the only reason this change exists, and it is invisible
783	// to the compiler and to every existing test: deleting it left the whole suite
784	// green, because the position still gets stamped by the ordinary success path
785	// (err == nil), so the only casualties were the counter and the log. Those are
786	// exactly the signal COR-1300 was filed to produce, and they would have gone
787	// quiet with nothing failing.
788	//
789	// Takes the span from ctx rather than as a parameter so a test can call it with
790	// a plain context and get a no-op span, matching the replicate-thunk seam
791	// recoverDefaultBranchRename already uses for the same reason.
792	func (s *syncer) reportSyncSuccess(ctx context.Context, result gitsync.SyncResult, req syncRequest) {
793		if result.Execution.Converged {
794			// Source asserted empty, target asserted empty, and git-sync
795			// corroborated both in one session: converged with nothing to apply.
796			// Reported as a real success rather than a no-op BECAUSE the coverage
797			// is provable, which is what lets the completion carry a write
798			// position — the thing that clears a resync flag on a repo that was
799			// created and never pushed to.
800			trace.SpanFromContext(ctx).SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.converged", true))
801			s.metrics.recordEmptySource(ctx, emptyReasonConverged, req.SourceClusterParent)
802			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Sync complete: source and target both empty, nothing to mirror",
803				slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
804				slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
805				slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
806			)
807			return
808		}
809		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Sync complete",
810			slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
811			slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
812			slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
813			slog.Int("applied", result.Counts.Applied),
814			slog.Int("skipped", result.Counts.Skipped),
815			slog.Int("blocked", result.Counts.Blocked),
816			slog.Int("deleted", result.Counts.Deleted),
817			// The strategy git-sync actually chose. Routing decisions (replicate
818			// vs bootstrap vs bootstrap resume) were previously invisible here,
819			// which is why ENT-2054 took a code read instead of a log query.
820			slog.String("operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
821			slog.String("transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
822			slog.String("relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
823		)
824	}

826	// refScopeFor builds the ref scope for one request. Extracted alongside
827	// syncPolicyFor because AllRefs is not merely this worker's preference: it is a
828	// precondition git-sync enforces for the empty-source policy (under a narrower
829	// scope the source listing is itself narrowed, so an empty result says nothing
830	// about the repository), and a scope built inline in the config literal is one
831	// no test can read.
832	func refScopeFor(req syncRequest) gitsync.RefScope {
833		return gitsync.RefScope{
834			AllRefs: true,
835			// refs/pull/* is GitHub's PR ref namespace — skip mirroring it
836			// to avoid surfacing source-side PR state on the mirror.
837			//
838			// refs/heads/trunk-merge/* and refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/*
839			// are ephemeral merge-queue refs (trunk-merge keyed by PR number
840			// + a per-attempt UUID; gh-readonly-queue is GitHub's native
841			// merge-queue namespace, refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/<base>/
842			// pr-<n>-<sha>): created and deleted within minutes, so mirroring
843			// them is pure churn. Because each is brand-new, git-sync plans a
844			// create (target hash zero) that races a concurrent webhook or the
845			// re-kicker and draws entire-server's create-side CAS rejection
846			// ("already exists"). They carry no value on the mirror, so we drop
847			// them at the source rather than push and prune the churn. (The
848			// create-race misclassification itself is now fixed upstream:
849			// git-sync classifies "already exists" as ErrTargetRefMoved — the
850			// create-side analog of "remote ref has changed" — so a create race
851			// that still slips through routes to dispositionRaced like any
852			// concurrent-ref miss rather than a hard sync failure; see
853			// isConcurrentRefError. This exclusion just removes the dominant
854			// source of those redeliveries.)
855			//
856			// The remaining prefixes mirror entiredb's reserved-push denylist
857			// (the reservedPrefixes/reservedExact sets in its refpolicy
858			// package, applied by server/githttp receive-pack):
859			// git-receive-pack returns 403 "push to <ref> is not allowed"
860			// for any of these namespaces. Under AllRefs we faithfully copy
861			// whatever the source advertises, so a stray ref like
862			// refs/remotes/origin/* accidentally pushed up to a source repo
863			// would otherwise fail the entire sync permanently. Excluding
864			// the prefixes here means we neither read them from the source
865			// nor try to push/prune them on the target.
866			//
867			// refs/tlog/* is entiredb-owned (commit-tlog state appended by
868			// entire-server on its receive-pack hook); direct pushes are
869			// rejected with "use sync instead".
870			//
871			// Per-kind: an entiredb source (native mirroring) additionally
872			// syncs the unmirrored namespace — see excludeRefPrefixesFor.
873			ExcludeRefPrefixes: excludeRefPrefixesFor(req.kind()),
874			// Exact-match reservations (not prefixes): skip the bare
875			// directory-anchor refs entiredb blocks, without excluding
876			// their mirrored children (refs/heads/entire/a still syncs).
877			ExcludeRefs: excludeRefsFor(req.kind()),
878			// The namespace kind is scoped by inclusion: every ref outside the
879			// Entire-owned namespace is neither pushed nor pruned, whatever the
880			// payload claims.
881			IncludeRefPrefixes: includeRefPrefixesFor(req.kind()),
882		}
883	}
884	
885	// syncPolicyFor builds the git-sync policy for one request. Extracted from the
886	// config literal so the empty-source wiring is unit-testable: every field here
887	// is a plain bool with a defaulted-off zero value, so dropping any one of them
888	// compiles, passes, and silently turns the policy off — which is exactly how
889	// the first version of this shipped inert (AllowEmptySource set, the two
890	// assertions it requires never supplied).
891	func syncPolicyFor(req syncRequest) gitsync.SyncPolicy {
892		// entiredb-kind only, for both halves of the empty-source policy. The
893		// distinction is only sound where a data plane can answer for the
894		// repository's ref state, and the watermark it feeds exists solely for
895		// native mirrors — a GitHub source gains nothing and would have its
896		// empty-repo syncs reclassified from no-op to ref-applying success,
897		// moving last_success_unix and pruning the failure index on a sync that
898		// applied nothing.
899		// The namespace kind is excluded with GitHub: it takes no position
900		// snapshot, so it can assert nothing about either leg.
901		native := req.kind() == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB
902		return gitsync.SyncPolicy{
903			IncludeTags: true,
904			Prune:       true,
905			// Ask git-sync to separate "the source has no refs" from "the scope
906			// selected none of them", and to treat a source and target both
907			// VERIFIED empty as the converged state they are rather than an
908			// error. That converged sync stamps a write position, which is what
909			// lets entire-core's resync sweep clear a flag on a repo that was
910			// created and never pushed to (COR-1300); without it the placement is
911			// flagged behind forever, since a no-op completion carries no
912			// watermark and the flag can never be satisfied.
913			AllowEmptySource: native,
914			// An owner that deleted its last namespace branch advertises refs but
915			// none in scope; without this the replicas keep serving a branch the
916			// owner no longer has.
917			AllowEmptyScope: req.namespaceScoped(),
918			// The assertions git-sync requires before it will call anything
919			// converged: it cannot determine emptiness itself on either leg,
920			// because ref hiding is invisible to a client and configured
921			// independently per leg, so an empty advertisement and a repository
922			// full of hidden refs are the same observation. They come from
923			// RepoAdmin.GetWritePosition on each side, read before the fetch (see
924			// syncRequest).
925			//
926			// git-sync treats them as necessary and never sufficient: it still
927			// requires an empty advertisement on each leg, an unborn HEAD on the
928			// source, and no visible in-scope target ref, and each of those checks
929			// can only refuse. So a wrong assertion cannot manufacture a
930			// convergence out of a populated repository — but a MISSING one
931			// (every read failure lands there) does forfeit a real convergence,
932			// which is the direction to fail in.
933			//
934			// Gated on native as well, so a GitHub request carrying stray
935			// assertions cannot half-enable a policy whose other half is off.
936			SourceAssertedEmpty: native && req.sourceAssertedEmpty(),
937			TargetAssertedEmpty: native && req.targetAssertedEmpty(),
938		}
939	}

941	func (s *syncer) targetURL(req syncRequest) string {
942		return fmt.Sprintf("%s/git/repo/%s", s.targetBaseURL, req.TargetULID)
943	}

945	// sourceAuth returns a gitsync.AuthProvider for the source endpoint.
946	// entiredb sources never mint: the worker's client certificate is the whole
947	// credential (the source cluster's svctok listener grants the workload
948	// cert-only cluster-wide pull), and clusterTransport already routes the
949	// fetch onto the mTLS round-tripper — a nil provider attaches no header.
950	// For GitHub, returns nil when the job has no installation ID or the App
951	// client is not configured — callers fall through to anonymous GitHub
952	// access for public repos.
953	func (s *syncer) sourceAuth(ctx context.Context, req syncRequest) (gitsync.AuthProvider, error) {
954		if req.entiredbSourced() {
955			return nil, nil
956		}
957		if req.InstallationID == 0 || s.githubApp == nil {
958			return nil, nil
959		}
960	
961		ctx, span := Tracer().Start(ctx, "mirror.source_auth",
962			trace.WithAttributes(
963				attribute.Int64("entire.installation_id", req.InstallationID),
964				attribute.String("entire.source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
965			),
966		)
967		defer span.End()
968	
969		// Time exactly the mint round-trip. This is the most actionable git-op
970		// breakdown leg (a synchronous entire-core STS call on every authenticated
971		// sync) and the before/after baseline for COR-596 token caching. Tagged
972		// ok|error only — the failure breakdown lives on this span, not the metric.
973		start := time.Now()
974		token, err := s.githubApp.InstallationToken(ctx, req.TargetULID, req.SourceOwner, req.SourceRepo, req.InstallationID)
975		if err != nil {
976			s.metrics.recordSourceAuth(ctx, sourceAuthOutcomeError, time.Since(start))
977			span.RecordError(err)
978			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "installation token")
979			// Returned unwrapped exactly as before: the sole caller (sync) wraps it
980			// with "resolving source auth: %w" and runs it through classifySyncError,
981			// and the token-leak guard (TestSyncDoesNotLeakInstallationToken) depends
982			// on that path — re-wrapping here would change the error text under it for
983			// no benefit.
984			return nil, err
985		}
986		s.metrics.recordSourceAuth(ctx, sourceAuthOutcomeOK, time.Since(start))
987		return gitsync.StaticAuthProvider{
988			Source: gitsync.EndpointAuth{Username: "x-access-token", Token: token},
989		}, nil
990	}

1	// Package failindex maintains the mirror-sync failure index: a JetStream KV
2	// bucket that records repos whose git-sync terminally failed, keyed by the
3	// entiredb mirror ULID, so a paced re-kicker can re-drive them. See
4	// docs/design/mirror-sync-failure-index.md.
5	//
6	// The worker is the sole writer: RecordFailure on a terminal failure (a CAS
7	// upsert with a per-repo attempt counter, deduplicated by the originating
8	// stream sequence), and ClearOnSuccess when a later sync for the repo succeeds.
9	// The package depends only on nats.go and stores the original job subject and
10	// payload verbatim — it never decodes them — so it stays out of the gen/proto
11	// import graph (the dependency that reverted #109).
12	package failindex
13	
14	import (
15		"context"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19		"time"
20	
21		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
22		"github.com/nats-io/nuid"
23	)
24	
25	// Version1 is the current FailedSync schema version.
26	const Version1 = 1
27	
28	// DefaultBucket is the KV bucket name, declared in fleet (apps/nats-streams).
29	const DefaultBucket = "mirror_sync_failed"
30	
31	// RekickHeader is the NATS header the re-kicker (cmd/rekicker) stamps on a
32	// re-emitted job. The worker reads it on a successful sync to tag the clear
33	// cleared{via=rekick} vs cleared{via=normal}. It is ONLY a metric tag —
34	// clearing happens on any success regardless — so the index never depends on
35	// the re-kicker to prune repos that healed on their own. Shared here because
36	// both cmd/worker (reader) and cmd/rekicker (writer) need the exact string.
37	const RekickHeader = "Mirror-Rekick"
38	
39	// RekickMsg builds the re-emit message for a stored failure: the stored job
40	// payload republished verbatim to its stored subject, stamped with
41	// RekickHeader (so the worker tags the eventual clear as via=rekick) and a
42	// FRESH Nats-Msg-Id (so the re-emit is NOT collapsed by the stream's dedup
43	// window against the original or a prior re-kick — it must be delivered and
44	// retried). Shared by the automated re-kicker (cmd/rekicker) and the operator
45	// CLI (mirror-pipeline-admin failindex rekick) so the two cannot drift on the
46	// wire contract.
47	func RekickMsg(ulid string, fs FailedSync) *nats.Msg {
48		msg := nats.NewMsg(fs.Subject)
49		msg.Data = fs.Payload
50		msg.Header.Set(RekickHeader, ulid)
51		msg.Header.Set(nats.MsgIdHdr, nuid.Next())
52		return msg
53	}
54	
55	// FailureReason classifies why a job was dead-ended (low cardinality).
56	type FailureReason string
57	
58	const (
59		ReasonPermanent     FailureReason = "permanent"      // a permanent sync error
60		ReasonMaxDeliveries FailureReason = "max_deliveries" // exhausted the consumer's MaxDeliver
61		ReasonValidation    FailureReason = "validation"     // a pre-sync validation reject
62	)
63	
64	// Source identifies the code path that recorded the entry (low cardinality).
65	const (
66		SourceWorkerCompletion = "worker_completion" // sync succeeded; ready publication exhausted deliveries
67		SourceWorkerPermanent  = "worker_permanent"
68		SourceWorkerValidation = "worker_validation"
69		SourceWorkerExhausted  = "worker_exhausted" // MaxDeliver exhausted (in-process pre-emption)
70		SourceAdvisory         = "advisory"         // the MAX_DELIVERIES/MSG_TERMINATED backstop
71	)
72	
73	// CorruptOp identifies which write path hit a stored entry whose JSON could not
74	// be unmarshalled (corruption, or a pre-Version1 schema). Both paths are
75	// fail-safe — RecordFailure overwrites the bad entry fresh, ClearOnSuccess
76	// leaves it untouched — but that recovery is otherwise invisible, so the worker
77	// wires a handler (WithCorruptHandler) to count + log it.
78	type CorruptOp string
79	
80	const (
81		// CorruptOpRecord: RecordFailure found an unreadable entry and overwrote it
82		// fresh — the repo's prior Attempts / FirstSeen triage history is lost.
83		CorruptOpRecord CorruptOp = "record"
84		// CorruptOpClear: ClearOnSuccess found an unreadable entry and left it in
85		// place (it can't prove the success is newer than the recorded failure).
86		CorruptOpClear CorruptOp = "clear"
87	)
88	
89	// FailedSync is the value stored per repo (keyed by mirror ULID). Subject +
90	// Payload are enough to republish an exact-equivalent job; the rest is triage
91	// metadata. LastSeq is the originating mirror_git_v1 stream sequence of the
92	// last counted failure — the dedup token that makes Attempts count distinct
93	// failing jobs rather than distinct writes.
94	type FailedSync struct {
95		Version   int           `json:"version"`
96		Subject   string        `json:"subject"`
97		Payload   []byte        `json:"payload"`
98		Reason    FailureReason `json:"reason"`
99		Source    string        `json:"source"`
100		LastError string        `json:"last_error,omitempty"`
101		Attempts  int           `json:"attempts"`
102		LastSeq   uint64        `json:"last_seq"`
103		FirstSeen time.Time     `json:"first_seen"`
104		LastSeen  time.Time     `json:"last_seen"`
105	}
106	
107	// kvStore is the subset of nats.KeyValue the index uses; it is the test seam.
108	type kvStore interface {
109		Get(key string) (nats.KeyValueEntry, error)
110		Create(key string, value []byte) (uint64, error)
111		Update(key string, value []byte, last uint64) (uint64, error)
112		Delete(key string, opts ...nats.DeleteOpt) error
113		WatchAll(opts ...nats.WatchOpt) (nats.KeyWatcher, error)
114	}
115	
116	// defaultCASRetries bounds the optimistic-concurrency retry loop. Several writers
117	// can target one repo key at once: a worker replica's in-process write plus the
118	// advisory backstop, which fans its delivery out across a worker pool. A few
119	// retries is still ample — a committed Update raises LastSeq, so every lower-seq
120	// writer then short-circuits on the seq<=LastSeq no-op instead of retrying, and
121	// same-repo jobs are collapsed within the publish-time dedup window, so same-key
122	// contention stays well under the budget in practice.
123	const defaultCASRetries = 5
124	
125	// Index is the failure index, bound to an existing KV bucket.
126	type Index struct {
127		kv         kvStore
128		casRetries int
129		// onCorrupt, when set, is called whenever a write path hits an unreadable
130		// stored entry (see CorruptOp). nil by default; wired via WithCorruptHandler.
131		onCorrupt func(ulid string, op CorruptOp)
132	}
133	
134	// Option configures an Index at Open time.
135	type Option func(*Index)
136	
137	// WithCorruptHandler registers a callback invoked whenever a write path hits an
138	// unreadable stored entry (see CorruptOp). It keeps this package free of any
139	// metrics/logging dependency: the worker passes a handler that increments
140	// mirror.sync.failed_index.corrupt_reset{op} and logs the ULID. The handler runs
141	// inline on the write path, so it must be cheap and non-blocking.
142	func WithCorruptHandler(fn func(ulid string, op CorruptOp)) Option {
143		return func(ix *Index) { ix.onCorrupt = fn }
144	}
145	
146	// WithMaxEntryAge is retained for source compatibility.
147	// Deprecated: unresolved failures no longer expire; bound retries in the reader.
148	func WithMaxEntryAge(time.Duration) Option { return func(*Index) {} }
149	
150	// WithEvictHandler is retained for source compatibility.
151	// Deprecated: unresolved failures are never evicted by age.
152	func WithEvictHandler(func(string, time.Duration)) Option { return func(*Index) {} }
153	
154	// Open binds to the KV bucket, which must already exist — it is declared in
155	// fleet (apps/nats-streams) and reconciled by nack; binaries never create it.
156	func Open(js nats.JetStreamContext, bucket string, opts ...Option) (*Index, error) {
157		kv, err := js.KeyValue(bucket)
158		if err != nil {
159			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failindex: bind kv bucket %q: %w", bucket, err)
160		}
161		ix := &Index{kv: kv, casRetries: defaultCASRetries}
162		for _, opt := range opts {
163			opt(ix)
164		}
165		return ix, nil
166	}
167	
168	// RecordFailure upserts the entry for ulid, incrementing Attempts once per
169	// distinct originating sequence (seq). It is idempotent for a repeated
170	// (ulid, seq), so the in-process path and the advisory backstop recording the
171	// same terminal failure do not double-count. fs supplies Subject, Payload,
172	// Reason and Source; the counter and timestamp fields are managed here. now is
173	// injected for testability.
174	//
175	// recorded reports whether this call actually created or updated an entry. It is
176	// false on a dedup/reorder no-op (seq <= LastSeq), where the failure was already
177	// captured by an earlier or concurrent write. Callers should increment their
178	// "recorded" metric only when recorded is true, so a redelivery (or the
179	// in-process/advisory pair) doesn't inflate it. On a non-nil error nothing was
180	// written and recorded is false.
181	func (ix *Index) RecordFailure(ulid string, fs FailedSync, seq uint64, now time.Time) (recorded bool, err error) {
182		return ix.recordFailure(ulid, fs, seq, now, false)
183	}
184	
185	// RecordNoopCompletionFailure captures a failed ready publication after a noop.
186	// A noop does not reconcile refs: preserve any existing non-completion failure
187	// (including unreadable evidence) instead of making it eligible for noop cleanup.
188	func (ix *Index) RecordNoopCompletionFailure(ulid string, fs FailedSync, seq uint64, now time.Time) (bool, error) {
189		if fs.Source != SourceWorkerCompletion {
190			return false, errors.New("failindex: noop completion must use worker_completion source")
191		}
192		return ix.recordFailure(ulid, fs, seq, now, true)
193	}
194	
195	func (ix *Index) recordFailure(ulid string, fs FailedSync, seq uint64, now time.Time, preserveSyncFailure bool) (recorded bool, err error) {
196		if ulid == "" {
197			return false, errors.New("failindex: empty ulid")
198		}
199		for attempt := 0; attempt <= ix.casRetries; attempt++ {
200			entry, gErr := ix.kv.Get(ulid)
201			switch {
202			case errors.Is(gErr, nats.ErrKeyNotFound):
203				v := fs
204				v.Version = Version1
205				v.Attempts = 1
206				v.LastSeq = seq
207				v.FirstSeen = now
208				v.LastSeen = now
209				data, mErr := json.Marshal(v)
210				if mErr != nil {
211					return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: marshal %s: %w", ulid, mErr)
212				}
213				if _, cErr := ix.kv.Create(ulid, data); cErr != nil {
214					if errors.Is(cErr, nats.ErrKeyExists) {
215						continue // a concurrent writer created it first — retry as update
216					}
217					return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: create %s: %w", ulid, cErr)
218				}
219				return true, nil
220			case gErr != nil:
221				return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: get %s: %w", ulid, gErr)
222			}
223	
224			var cur FailedSync
225			corrupt := false
226			if uErr := json.Unmarshal(entry.Value(), &cur); uErr != nil {
227				// Unreadable entry (corruption / older schema): start fresh rather
228				// than wedge — the CAS Update below still guards the write. Defer the
229				// onCorrupt report until the overwrite actually commits: a reset entry
230				// has LastSeq 0, so a degenerate seq==0 call would otherwise report a
231				// reset the no-op below never performed.
232				cur = FailedSync{FirstSeen: now}
233				corrupt = true
234			}
235			if preserveSyncFailure && (corrupt || cur.Source != SourceWorkerCompletion) {
236				return false, nil
237			}
238			if seq <= cur.LastSeq {
239				// Already counted (== — the in-process path and the advisory backstop
240				// recording the same message), or an out-of-order OLDER failure (< —
241				// a lower-seq same-repo job recorded after a higher-seq one, possible
242				// across concurrent worker replicas). Never move LastSeq backwards:
243				// ClearOnSuccess trusts it as "the newest recorded failure", so a
244				// regressed LastSeq would let an intermediate success wipe a newer
245				// failure from the index. Stream seqs are monotonic, so the newest
246				// failure always has the highest seq. (Attempts under-counts the rare
247				// reorder — acceptable; it is triage-only.) No new entry → recorded=false.
248				return false, nil
249			}
250			cur.Version = Version1
251			cur.Subject = fs.Subject
252			cur.Payload = fs.Payload
253			cur.Reason = fs.Reason
254			cur.Source = fs.Source
255			cur.LastError = fs.LastError
256			cur.Attempts++
257			cur.LastSeq = seq
258			cur.LastSeen = now
259			if cur.FirstSeen.IsZero() {
260				cur.FirstSeen = now
261			}
262			data, mErr := json.Marshal(cur)
263			if mErr != nil {
264				return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: marshal %s: %w", ulid, mErr)
265			}
266			if _, uErr := ix.kv.Update(ulid, data, entry.Revision()); uErr != nil {
267				if errors.Is(uErr, nats.ErrKeyExists) {
268					continue // CAS conflict — another write landed; re-read and retry
269				}
270				return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: update %s: %w", ulid, uErr)
271			}
272			if corrupt && ix.onCorrupt != nil {
273				// The unreadable entry was actually overwritten just now — its prior
274				// Attempts/FirstSeen history is lost, so surface it. Fires exactly once
275				// per call (this is the sole success path), and never on the seq<=LastSeq
276				// no-op or a CAS-conflict retry that re-reads a readable entry.
277				ix.onCorrupt(ulid, CorruptOpRecord)
278			}
279			return true, nil
280		}
281		return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: record %s exhausted %d CAS retries", ulid, ix.casRetries)
282	}
283	
284	// ClearOnSuccess removes the entry for ulid after a successful sync, provided
285	// the success is at least as new as the last recorded failure (successSeq >=
286	// LastSeq) so an older success cannot wipe a newer recorded failure. It is a
287	// no-op when the repo is not in the index (the common case). The delete is
288	// revision-guarded, so a failure write that lands between the Get and the
289	// Delete is preserved. Returns whether an entry was actually removed (for the
290	// cleared{via} metric). Clearing is best-effort: callers should log an error
291	// but must not fail the sync (it already succeeded; a stale entry self-heals on
292	// the next success or re-kick).
293	func (ix *Index) ClearOnSuccess(ulid string, successSeq uint64) (bool, error) {
294		return ix.clearOnSuccess(ulid, successSeq, false)
295	}
296	
297	// ClearOnCompletion removes only a completion-publication failure after a ready
298	// publication succeeds. The source and sequence checks use the same KV revision
299	// as the conditional delete, so a concurrent sync failure cannot be erased.
300	func (ix *Index) ClearOnCompletion(ulid string, successSeq uint64) (bool, error) {
301		return ix.clearOnSuccess(ulid, successSeq, true)
302	}
303	
304	func (ix *Index) clearOnSuccess(ulid string, successSeq uint64, completionOnly bool) (bool, error) {
305		if ulid == "" {
306			return false, errors.New("failindex: empty ulid")
307		}
308		entry, err := ix.kv.Get(ulid)
309		if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrKeyNotFound) {
310			return false, nil
311		}
312		if err != nil {
313			return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: get %s: %w", ulid, err)
314		}
315		var cur FailedSync
316		if uErr := json.Unmarshal(entry.Value(), &cur); uErr != nil {
317			// Unreadable entry: we can't verify this success is newer than the
318			// recorded failure, so don't delete it on a possibly-older success —
319			// leave it for RecordFailure to overwrite (which recovers from
320			// corruption) or for explicit cleanup. The clear path must not be the
321			// one that destroys a corrupt-but-possibly-newer entry.
322			if ix.onCorrupt != nil {
323				ix.onCorrupt(ulid, CorruptOpClear)
324			}
325			return false, nil
326		}
327		if completionOnly && cur.Source != SourceWorkerCompletion {
328			return false, nil
329		}
330		if successSeq < cur.LastSeq {
331			return false, nil // a newer failure is recorded — leave it for its own success
332		}
333		if dErr := ix.kv.Delete(ulid, nats.LastRevision(entry.Revision())); dErr != nil {
334			if errors.Is(dErr, nats.ErrKeyExists) {
335				return false, nil // revision moved under us — a newer write won; skip
336			}
337			return false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: delete %s: %w", ulid, dErr)
338		}
339		return true, nil
340	}
341	
342	// Keys returns the ULIDs currently held in the index — live keys only
343	// (tombstones from cleared repos are excluded). An empty index returns an empty
344	// slice and a nil error. The re-kicker (PR 2) lists these and re-drives each so
345	// stuck repos re-sync and self-clear.
346	//
347	// ctx bounds the listing. nats.go's KeyValue.Keys() takes no context, and a
348	// WatchAll replay over a large index is unbounded — so without this the
349	// re-kicker's pass deadline / SIGTERM could not interrupt the listing, which
350	// runs before the publish loop and is slowest exactly when the index is largest
351	// (post-outage). We drive the watcher directly and bail on ctx.Done(); Stop()
352	// removes the server-side ephemeral consumer on every return (a client dispatch
353	// goroutine left blocked on the watcher's internal buffer after a mid-stream
354	// cancel of a >256-key listing is reclaimed at process exit — safe because the
355	// re-kicker is a run-to-completion CronJob; drain w.Updates() after Stop() if
356	// ever reused in a long-lived process). Read path: needs $JS.API.> (watch
357	// consumer-create + direct get) + SUBSCRIBE _INBOX.> (delivery), no $KV write.
358	func (ix *Index) Keys(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
359		// IgnoreDeletes + MetaOnly mirror nats.go's own Keys(): live keys only, no
360		// payload fetch.
361		w, err := ix.kv.WatchAll(nats.IgnoreDeletes(), nats.MetaOnly())
362		if err != nil {
363			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failindex: watch keys: %w", err)
364		}
365		defer func() { _ = w.Stop() }()
366	
367		var keys []string
368		// onSentinel handles nats.go's explicit nil "initial set fully delivered"
369		// sentinel — the ONLY signal that denotes a genuinely complete listing. A
370		// stalled replay enqueues ErrKeyWatcherTimeout on Error() BEFORE that sentinel
371		// (the lone path that ever writes the watcher's errCh), so surface it as an
372		// incomplete listing; otherwise the keys collected so far ARE the whole live
373		// index. (A bare channel close WITHOUT a sentinel is handled separately below.)
374		onSentinel := func() ([]string, error) {
375			if werr := watcherErr(w); werr != nil {
376				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failindex: keys: incomplete listing: %w", werr)
377			}
378			return keys, nil
379		}
380	
381		for {
382			select {
383			case <-ctx.Done():
384				// Deadline / SIGTERM fired. Don't discard a listing that ALSO just
385				// completed (sentinel queued) to a simultaneous cancel — select picks
386				// randomly among ready cases. Drain one item: ONLY the explicit nil
387				// sentinel means the initial set was fully delivered (return the keys); a
388				// real entry, or a bare channel close, means it wasn't complete, so honor
389				// the cancellation (the keys are an incomplete prefix and must be dropped).
390				select {
391				case entry, ok := <-w.Updates():
392					if ok && entry == nil {
393						return onSentinel()
394					}
395				default:
396				}
397				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failindex: keys: %w", ctx.Err())
398			case entry, ok := <-w.Updates():
399				if !ok {
400					// Updates closed WITHOUT a preceding nil sentinel: nats.go's pDone tore
401					// the watcher down mid-listing (connection drop / reconnect exhaustion /
402					// a non-retryable ordered-consumer recreate) and Stopped the init timer
403					// first, so errCh is closed EMPTY — the close itself is the only
404					// incompleteness signal (a normal/timed-out completion always delivers a
405					// sentinel first, so we'd have returned via onSentinel). Returning the
406					// prefix collected so far as the whole index would starve the tail on
407					// re-kick while exiting healthy, so fail the listing loud — the next
408					// tick retries.
409					return nil, fmt.Errorf("failindex: keys: incomplete listing: watcher closed before the initial set completed (%d keys collected)", len(keys))
410				}
411				if entry == nil {
412					return onSentinel()
413				}
414				keys = append(keys, entry.Key())
415			}
416		}
417	}
418	
419	// watcherErr non-blockingly reads a pending watcher error. nats.go's init timer
420	// enqueues ErrKeyWatcherTimeout on Error() BEFORE sending the nil sentinel, so
421	// once Keys observes the sentinel that error is already readable; a normal
422	// "caught up" completion leaves Error() empty. NB this is the ONLY path that
423	// writes errCh — a teardown-driven close (pDone) leaves it empty, which is why
424	// Keys treats a sentinel-less channel close as incomplete on its own.
425	func watcherErr(w nats.KeyWatcher) error {
426		select {
427		case err := <-w.Error():
428			return err
429		default:
430			return nil
431		}
432	}
433	
434	// Get returns the stored entry for ulid. found is false (with a nil error) when
435	// the repo is not in the index — e.g. it healed and was cleared between a Keys()
436	// listing and this read, which the re-kicker treats as a benign skip. A stored
437	// value that won't unmarshal returns an error: unlike the write paths (which
438	// overwrite a corrupt entry fresh), a reader has no fresh value to recover with.
439	func (ix *Index) Get(ulid string) (fs FailedSync, found bool, err error) {
440		fs, _, found, err = ix.GetWithRevision(ulid)
441		if err != nil {
442			found = false
443		}
444		return
445	}
446	
447	// GetWithRevision returns the revision that must accompany an operator resolution.
448	func (ix *Index) GetWithRevision(ulid string) (FailedSync, uint64, bool, error) {
449		entry, err := ix.kv.Get(ulid)
450		if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrKeyNotFound) {
451			return FailedSync{}, 0, false, nil
452		}
453		if err != nil {
454			return FailedSync{}, 0, false, fmt.Errorf("failindex: get %s: %w", ulid, err)
455		}
456		var fs FailedSync
457		if err := json.Unmarshal(entry.Value(), &fs); err != nil {
458			return FailedSync{}, entry.Revision(), true, fmt.Errorf("failindex: unmarshal %s: %w", ulid, err)
459		}
460		return fs, entry.Revision(), true, nil
461	}
462	
463	// Resolve removes exactly the observation reviewed by an operator.
464	func (ix *Index) Resolve(ulid string, revision uint64) error {
465		if ulid == "" || revision == 0 {
466			return errors.New("failindex: key and nonzero revision required")
467		}
468		if err := ix.kv.Delete(ulid, nats.LastRevision(revision)); err != nil {
469			return fmt.Errorf("failindex: resolve %s revision %d: %w", ulid, revision, err)
470		}
471		return nil
472	}
473	
474	// Delete unconditionally removes the entry for ulid. Unlike ClearOnSuccess (the
475	// worker's seq/revision-guarded prune after a real sync), this is the operator
476	// escape hatch — used by mirror-pipeline-admin to drop an entry by hand, e.g. a
477	// repo that is genuinely gone but keeps the index occupied, or a corrupt entry a
478	// reader can't decode. It takes no guard on purpose: the operator's intent wins
479	// over any concurrent write. Deleting a key that is not present is a no-op (nil
480	// error), so a double-delete is harmless. Note the entry can legitimately
481	// reappear: if the repo is still receiving traffic and failing, the worker's
482	// next RecordFailure re-creates it fresh — which is correct (an actively-failing
483	// repo shouldn't be silently abandoned; evict the workload first, then delete).
484	func (ix *Index) Delete(ulid string) error {
485		if ulid == "" {
486			return errors.New("failindex: empty ulid")
487		}
488		if err := ix.kv.Delete(ulid); err != nil {
489			return fmt.Errorf("failindex: delete %s: %w", ulid, err)
490		}
491		return nil
492	}

# KV_mirror_sync_failed — the mirror-sync failure index (L1 recovery).
#
# Lives in EVERY NATS cluster (base/): cmd/worker writes an entry per repo whose
# git-sync terminally fails (permanent error / MaxDeliver-exhausted), keyed by
# the entiredb mirror ULID, and deletes it when a later sync for that repo
# succeeds. A paced re-kicker (PR 2) re-drives the entries.
# See mirror-pipeline/docs/design/mirror-sync-failure-index.md.
#
# Reconciled by nack in control-loop mode (the KeyValue CRD is control-loop
# only — enabled fleet-wide via apps/nats-jetstream-controller). history=1 →
# last-write-wins; values and deletion markers consume the byte budget. The binary binds (KeyValue(bucket)); it never
# creates the bucket, matching the declarative-ownership model (see README.md).
apiVersion: jetstream.nats.io/v1beta2
kind: KeyValue
metadata:
  name: kv-mirror-sync-failed
spec:
  bucket: mirror_sync_failed
  # Flux runs prune: true — without this, deleting or renaming this CR would
  # make nack DELETE the live bucket (and every recorded failure). Guard it.
  preventDelete: true
  history: 1 # one latest value or deletion marker per key
  storage: file
  replicas: 3
  ttl: 0s # retain unresolved failures; compact old deletion markers separately
  maxBytes: 1073741824 # 1 GiB — provisional ceiling (design doc open question #4)
---
